syntax.guarded_form: @p not.b32 d, a;  (alternatively @!p not.b32 d, a;)
syntax_notes: .b32 is listed in the not .type set; the bounded base form is the .b32 instantiation of 'not.type d, a;' (PTX-9.3-NOT-003; claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-005).

The other instruction types of the same section (.pred, .b16, .b64) are recorded as official source facts (PTX-9.3-NOT-003/009/010) but are out of the bounded base scope (architecture D-0c; claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-068).

The optional guard predicate is omitted from instruction-description syntax (section 9.7, PTX-9.3-NOT-013) but may prefix any PTX instruction as @{!}p (section 9.3, PTX-9.3-NOT-018); the general predication form is defined in section 9.7.13.2 (Control Flow Instructions: @), incl. 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-NOT-SEM1-028). The guarded_form spelling lists the two guard spellings; @p and @!p have opposite execution conditions (see guard_semantics) and are not semantically interchangeable.

roles.d: destination operand. For instructions that create a result value, d is the destination operand (section 9.2, PTX-9.3-NOT-015); not writes the bitwise complement of a to d ('d = ~a;', PTX-9.3-NOT-005). The destination is a register variable in the .reg state space for the bounded base form (the official example not.b32 mask,mask; uses register operands, PTX-9.3-NOT-009); the general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule permits '_' for some instructions, but its applicability to the scalar not.b32 form is an open question (PTX-NOT-SEM1-067).
roles.a: source operand. For the bounded base form, a is a register variable (official example PTX-9.3-NOT-009; description 'Invert the bits in a.', PTX-9.3-NOT-004). Whether a may be a constant immediate is not explicitly evidenced in the not section (bundle GAP-1; claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-066).

operand_forms_supported_by_evidence: destination register of type .b32 (PTX-9.3-NOT-009 shows not.b32 mask,mask; with two register operands)
source register (same example; the destination and source may be the same register)
destination bit bucket '_' per the general section 9.2 rule (PTX-9.3-NOT-016); scalar not.b32 applicability is an open question (PTX-NOT-SEM1-067)

source constant immediate: NOT supported by direct evidence in the not section; sibling family examples (or.b32 mask mask,0x00010001, PTX-9.3-NOT-011; xor.b16 d,x,0x0001;, PTX-9.3-NOT-012) show immediates in the same logic/shift family but do not resolve the not-specific question (bundle GAP-1, do_not_infer: true; claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-066)
operand_form_evidence_notes: PTX-9.3-NOT-003: syntax 'not.type d, a;' with .type = { .pred, .b16, .b32, .b64 }; establishes the two-operand ordering d, a.
PTX-9.3-NOT-004: 'Invert the bits in a.' establishes that the source operand a is read and its bits are inverted.
PTX-9.3-NOT-009: official example 'not.b32  mask,mask;' uses two register operands, showing the destination and source may be the same register; the .pred form is out of the bounded base scope.

PTX-9.3-NOT-015: 'For instructions that create a result value, the d operand is the destination operand, while a, b, and c are source operands.' and the '@p opcode d, a;' form; the d, a form matches not.b32.

types.operand_typing_rule: Operands d and a are typed .b32 or a type compatible with .b32 under the section 5.2.1 compatibility rules combined with the family size-matching rule ('The size of the operands must match, but not necessarily the type.', PTX-9.3-NOT-006): any 32-bit fundamental type is size-compatible. The exact formulation of the size-based compatibility rule for not.b32 operand typing is an open question (OQ-7; claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-071).
types.compatibility_rules: Operand types and sizes are checked against instruction types for compatibility. Two fundamental types are compatible if they have the same basic type and are the same size; signed and unsigned integer types are compatible if they have the same size; the bit-size type is compatible with any fundamental type of the same size.
types.notes: The logic/shift family is described as fundamentally untyped, performing bit-wise operations on operands of any type of the same size (PTX-9.3-NOT-010). The not Notes state 'Allowed types include predicates.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-006), but the .pred form is out of the bounded base scope (claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-068).

modifiers.statement: The scalar not syntax 'not.type d, a;' has no modifier position in the official syntax block (PTX-9.3-NOT-003). The bounded base not.b32 form therefore has no modifiers.

static_preconditions.description: Type well-formedness: the instruction type specifier .b32 is a valid bit-size fundamental type of 32-bit width.

Operand typing: operands d and a are size-compatible with instruction type .b32 (32-bit operands), consistent with the family rule 'The size of the operands must match, but not necessarily the type.' and the bit-size compatibility rule.
Destination membership: the destination operand d denotes a declared register variable in the .reg state space, or is the bit bucket '_' (if adopted; applicability open question PTX-NOT-SEM1-067).
Source form: the source operand a is a register variable; whether a may be a constant immediate is not evidenced in the not section (bundle GAP-1; claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-066).
Guard well-typedness: if a guard is present, it refers to a predicate register variable of type .pred in the register state space, optionally negated.
Version gating: base not (and therefore the bounded base not.b32 form) is introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.

dynamic_preconditions.description: No dynamic precondition is stated in the evidence for not.b32 (for example, no requirement on the values held by source operands, and no flag or status-register requirement). None is asserted.

state_reads.description: When a is a register, its current (pre-instruction) value is read from the value-register file; the description 'Invert the bits in a.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-004) and the Semantics 'd = ~a;' (PTX-9.3-NOT-005) require this read. Whether a may be a constant immediate is an open question (PTX-NOT-SEM1-066).

state_reads.component: guard predicate register p (when a guard is present)
state_reads.description: The value of the predicate register referenced by the guard is read to evaluate the complete guard expression. The general predication form of section 9.7.13.2 states execution occurs for threads whose guard predicate is True ('Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.', PTX-9.3-NOT-031), so the guard read is the predicate value used by that evaluation.

state_writes.component: destination register d (on execution with a real destination register)
state_writes.description: When the complete guard expression evaluates true and d is a register, the destination register d is updated with the bitwise complement of the value read from source operand a. Only the destination update required by the bounded semantics is proposed: no other value register, predicate register, carry flag, or status/condition-code component is written by the bounded base not.b32.

When the destination is the bit bucket '_', the general section 9.2 rule indicates the destination register is replaced by the bit bucket; the represented consequence is that no value register is written (the result is discarded). This is supported only to the strength of the general rule; scalar not.b32-specific demonstration is absent (open question PTX-NOT-SEM1-067).

state_writes.component: state when the complete guard expression evaluates false
state_writes.description: When the complete guard expression evaluates false, the represented consequence is that the instruction does not execute and no state component changes. This is a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION grounded in the explicit official clause of section 9.7.13.2: 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-031) with Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-NOT-032), applied to not.b32 through the general rules that all PTX instructions may be predicated (PTX-9.3-NOT-013) and that all instructions have an optional guard predicate prefix @{!}p (PTX-9.3-NOT-018). The state-level reading 'no state component changes' is the semantic interpretation of 'do nothing' and is recorded as DERIVED (confidence medium), subject to Gate B confirmation; the official clause itself is SOURCE_FACT (PTX-NOT-SEM1-028).

guard_semantics.guard_expression_representation: An optional guard prefix @{!}p appears after an @ symbol to the left of the opcode, where p is a predicate register variable of type .pred, optionally negated with '!'. No guard is present in the syntax-description form (the optional guard predicate is omitted from the syntax), but all PTX instructions may be predicated. The general predication form is defined in section 9.7.13.2 (Control Flow Instructions: @): '@{!}p instruction;' with Description 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-031) and Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-NOT-032).

guard_expression_evaluation.no_guard: The complete guard expression is true; the instruction is executed unconditionally ('Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.', PTX-9.3-NOT-018).
guard_expression_evaluation.at_p: @p: the complete guard expression is the value of predicate register p; execution occurs when p is true.
guard_expression_evaluation.at_bang_p: @!p: the complete guard expression is the logical negation of the value of predicate register p; execution occurs when p is false. The official example '@!p bra L1; // if False, branch over' (PTX-9.3-NOT-019) and the general predication example '@!p div.f32 ratio,x,y // avoid division by zero' (PTX-9.3-NOT-033) show the negated guard executing when the underlying predicate is false.
guard_expression_evaluation.execution_condition: Execution occurs if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true (general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction', PTX-9.3-NOT-032; section 9.3 'controls conditional execution', PTX-9.3-NOT-018). The underlying predicate value is not confused with the evaluated guard expression: for @!p, the guard expression is true exactly when the predicate value is false.

guard_semantics.guard_false_consequence: The represented consequence when the complete guard expression evaluates false is that the instruction does not execute and the state is unchanged. This is a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION (PTX-NOT-SEM1-035, confidence medium) grounded in the explicit official clause of section 9.7.13.2: 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-031), with Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-NOT-032), applied to not.b32 through 'All PTX instructions may be predicated' (PTX-9.3-NOT-013) and 'All instructions have an optional guard predicate' (PTX-9.3-NOT-018). The official do-nothing clause is SOURCE_FACT (PTX-NOT-SEM1-028); the state-level reading 'no state component changes' is the semantic interpretation of 'do nothing' and is recorded as DERIVED. This follows the mov.b32 Gate B lesson: the consequence is not presented as a human assumption.
guard_semantics.predication_exception: st.param and ld.param instructions used for argument passing cannot be predicated; this exception does not mention not and therefore does not restrict not.b32 predication (PTX-9.3-NOT-028; claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-025).

behavior.semantic_pseudocode_source: PTX-9.3-NOT-005 (the not Semantics block, which contains exactly this line: 'd = ~a;').
behavior.complement_rule: When not.b32 executes with a register source, the value written to the destination register d equals the bitwise complement of the value read from source a, computed over the 32-bit untyped .b32 value domain. This is derived from 'd = ~a;' (PTX-9.3-NOT-005), 'Bitwise negation; one's complement.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-002), 'Invert the bits in a.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-004), and the .b32 'Bits (untyped)' 32-bit type (PTX-9.3-NOT-021, PTX-9.3-NOT-023).
behavior.complement_rule_classification: DERIVED_INTERPRETATION (PTX-NOT-SEM1-033); the Semantics line itself is SOURCE_FACT (PTX-NOT-SEM1-032).
behavior.guard_true_behavior: When the complete guard expression evaluates true (including the no-guard case), the instruction executes: the pre-instruction value of source operand a is read, and the destination register d is updated with the bitwise complement of that value; if d is the bit bucket '_', no register is written (per the general rule, applicability open PTX-NOT-SEM1-067). Guard-true execution is consistent with the general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-NOT-032).
behavior.guard_false_behavior: When the complete guard expression evaluates false, the represented consequence is that the instruction does not execute and the state is unchanged; this is a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION (PTX-NOT-SEM1-035, confidence medium) grounded in the explicit official clause 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-031) and its Semantics (PTX-9.3-NOT-032), applied to not.b32 via the general predicability rules (PTX-9.3-NOT-013, PTX-9.3-NOT-018).
behavior.aliasing_read_before_write: Because the semantics is a bitwise complement (d = ~a;), the value of a is read before the destination update; the official example 'not.b32  mask,mask;' (PTX-9.3-NOT-009) directly shows the destination and source may be the same register, in which case the register retains its pre-instruction value as the source of the complement (read-before-write makes the operation self-consistent).
behavior.determinism_note: Determinism is not explicitly stated in the source (bundle GAP-3); the execution relation for not.b32 is derived to be deterministic because the value written is fully determined by the value read (bitwise complement of a fixed 32-bit value, no arithmetic, no truncation, no rounding) and the guard evaluation is a deterministic function of the predicate register value. See the determinism section and PTX-NOT-SEM1-047.

exceptional_behavior.statement: No explicit error, trap, or exceptional-behavior clause for not (or not.b32) was found in the evidence (bundle coverage area 15 status NOT_FOUND; GAP-4). This absence is not asserted as a positive source fact that no exceptional behavior exists; no error, trap, or exceptional behavior is invented. Whether the absence means no such behaviors exist is recorded as an open question.

undefined_behavior.statement: No explicit undefined-behavior clause for not (or not.b32) was found in the evidence (GAP-4). No undefined-behavior claim is made; no undefined behavior is invented.

implementation_defined_behavior.statement: No explicit implementation-defined-behavior clause for not (or not.b32) was found in the evidence. No implementation-defined-behavior claim is made; no implementation-defined behavior is invented.

determinism.statement: The execution relation for not.b32 is deterministic: for any well-formed state and well-typed not.b32 instruction, the fully-specified rules determine at most one resulting state. The guard evaluation is a deterministic function of the predicate register value; the value written is exactly the bitwise complement of the value read (a pure 32-bit bit-wise operation, no arithmetic, no truncation, no rounding); and the only state write on execution is the destination update. Determinism is NOT explicitly stated in the source (bundle gap GAP-3; architecture assumption A-3); it is a derived interpretation stated as proof obligation PRF-1.

version_restrictions.base_not_b32_introduced_in: PTX ISA version 1.0 (the PTX ISA Notes of the not section state 'Introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.', PTX-9.3-NOT-007; not.b32 is a base not form).

target_restrictions.base_not_b32_restriction: No family-specific target restriction is stated for not; the Target ISA Notes of the not section state 'Supported on all target architectures.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-008), which directly establishes the not-family (and therefore not.b32) target set. Unlike the scalar mov.b32 case, no target-set gap exists for not.b32 because the 'Supported on all target architectures.' sentence is present in the not section itself (section 9.7.8.4).

version_and_target.note: The general @ predication form has its own Target ISA Note 'Supported on all target architectures.' and PTX ISA Note 'Introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-032); those notes concern the general predication form and are recorded separately (claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-029). They do not substitute for the not-family notes, which are already directly present (PTX-9.3-NOT-007/008).

semantic_claims.statement: The construct identity is the not instruction family: PTX ISA 9.3 section 9.7.8.4 'Logic and Shift Instructions: not', HTML anchor logic-and-shift-instructions-not (HTML lines 14358-14361; PDF page 257).
Section 9.1 states that each PTX instruction is described by its name, format, semantics, and examples.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: The framing of the not Syntax/Semantics/Notes/Examples blocks as normative source content is an interpretation of the section's role, not part of the quoted text (semantic-critic v1 finding F-1 lesson applied: interpretive tails are kept out of SOURCE_FACT statements).

semantic_claims.statement: The bounded unit is the scalar 32-bit bit-size form 'not.type d, a;' with instruction type .b32 of the not instruction of section 9.7.8.4, per the human-approved architecture bounded-scope decision D-0c (approved at Gate A). The .pred, .b16, and .b64 forms of the same section are recorded as official source facts but are not commitments of the bounded base unit (D-24, OQ-4).
The exact not syntax is 'not.type d, a;' with .type = { .pred, .b16, .b32, .b64 }; the .b32 type specifier is in the not type set.
The bounded base syntax form is 'not.b32 d, a;', the .b32 instantiation of 'not.type d, a;'. The .b32 type specifier is in the not type set and .b32 is a 32-bit 'Bits (untyped)' fundamental type.

Section 9.2 states that PTX instructions generally have from zero to four operands plus an optional guard predicate appearing after an @ symbol to the left of the opcode, with forms including '@p opcode d, a;'; and that for instructions that create a result value, the d operand is the destination operand while a, b, and c are source operands.
The not description is 'Bitwise negation; one's complement.'
The not execution description is 'Invert the bits in a.'
The official not Examples block contains 'not.b32  mask,mask;' and 'not.pred  p,q;'.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: The .b32 example uses two register operands both named mask, showing the destination and source may be the same register (carried as DERIVED claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-065); the .pred form is out of the bounded base scope (claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-068).

semantic_claims.statement: For the bounded base unit, the source operand a is a register variable (evidenced by the official example 'not.b32  mask,mask;' and the description 'Invert the bits in a.'). Whether a may also be a constant immediate is not explicitly evidenced in the not section (bundle GAP-1; open question PTX-NOT-SEM1-066); sibling family immediate examples are recorded as source facts (PTX-9.3-NOT-011/012) but are not used to infer not's allowed operand forms (do_not_infer: true).
Section 9.2 states that for some instructions the destination operand is optional and a bit bucket operand denoted with an underscore (_) may be used in place of a destination register.

Whether the bit bucket '_' is a permitted destination for the scalar not.b32 form is not explicitly evidenced in the not section; only the general section 9.2 rule exists (bundle GAP-2; architecture OQ-2).
.b32 is a fundamental type specifier of basic type 'Bits (untyped)'; Table 8 lists .b8, .b16, .b32, .b64, .b128 under 'Bits (untyped)'.

A fundamental type specifies both a basic type and a size; register variables are always of a fundamental type; instructions operate on these types; the same type-size specifiers are used for variable definitions and instruction typing.

Registers (.reg state space) are fast storage locations; aside from 1-bit predicate registers, scalar registers have a width of 8-, 16-, 32-, 64-, or 128-bits (32-bit width is therefore possible for .b32 registers); registers are not fully addressable.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: '32-bit width is therefore possible for .b32 registers' is a direct reading of the listed widths, kept here for clarity; the remainder of the quote is verbatim.

semantic_claims.statement: Type compatibility: operand types and sizes are checked against instruction types for compatibility; two fundamental types are compatible if they have the same basic type and are the same size; signed and unsigned integer types are compatible if they have the same size; the bit-size type is compatible with any fundamental type having the same size.
The not Notes state: 'The size of the operands must match, but not necessarily the type.' and 'Allowed types include predicates.'
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: 'Allowed types include predicates' records the .pred form, which is out of the bounded base scope (claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-068); the size-matching sentence is the family operand-typing rule applied to the base form in claims PTX-NOT-SEM1-018/041.

semantic_claims.statement: The instruction type .b32 is the 'Bits (untyped)' fundamental type of width 32 bits; operands d and a are typed .b32 or a size-compatible 32-bit fundamental type under the family size-matching rule (PTX-9.3-NOT-006) combined with the bit-size compatibility rule (PTX-9.3-NOT-022); the exact formulation of the size-based compatibility rule is an open question (OQ-7; claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-071).

Section 9.7.8 intro states that the logic and shift instructions are fundamentally untyped, performing bit-wise operations on operands of any type, provided the operands are of the same size; that instructions and, or, xor, and not also operate on predicates; and the logical shift instruction list includes not.
The scalar not syntax has no modifier position; the bounded base not.b32 form has no modifiers (no .sat or other modifier exists in the not syntax block).
Section 9.7 states: 'All PTX instructions may be predicated. In the following descriptions, the optional guard predicate is omitted from the syntax.'

Section 9.3 states: 'All instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution of the instruction. The syntax to specify conditional execution is to prefix an instruction with @{!}p, where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated. Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.'
Section 9.3 states that predicate registers are virtual and have .pred as the type specifier, and can be declared as '.reg .pred p, q, r;'.
Section 9.3 shows official guard examples: '@p    add.s32      j, j, 1;' (guarded add) and '@!p   bra  L1;' (negated-guard branch).
Section 7.1 states: 'st.param and ld.param instructions used for argument passing cannot be predicated.'
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: The predication exception does not mention not, so the general predication applicability to not is not contradicted (guard_semantics.predication_exception).

semantic_claims.statement: Section 9.7.13 'Control Flow Instructions' lists the constructs '{} @ bra call ret exit' and states these PTX instructions and syntax are for controlling execution in a PTX program; the @ construct is listed among the control-flow constructs.

Section 9.7.13.1 'Control Flow Instructions: {}' states that '{ instructionList }' creates a group of instructions, used primarily for defining a function body, and also provides a mechanism for determining the scope of a variable.

Section 9.7.13.2 'Control Flow Instructions: @' explicitly defines the false-guard state effect for the general predication form: 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (HTML lines 21826-21839; PDF page 400).
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: This is the explicit official false-guard clause. The application of this clause to the bounded base not.b32 (guard-false consequence) is a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION recorded as claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-035 with the derivation chain in claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-031; the state-level reading 'no state component changes' is the interpretation of 'do nothing' and is subject to Gate B confirmation.

semantic_claims.statement: Section 9.7.13.2 Semantics line: 'If {!}p then instruction'. PTX ISA Notes for the general @ form: 'Introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.'; Target ISA Notes for the general @ form: 'Supported on all target architectures.'
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: The version and target notes in this fragment concern the general predication form, not the not.b32 scalar form's version/target set; the base form's own notes are recorded in claims PTX-NOT-SEM1-048/049 (PTX-9.3-NOT-007/008).

semantic_claims.statement: Section 9.7.13.2 Examples use the general guard forms: '@!p div.f32      ratio,x,y  // avoid division by zero' (negated guard guarding an instruction) and '@q  bra L23;                // conditional branch' (positive guard guarding a branch).

Derivation chain for not.b32 guard behavior: (1) 'All PTX instructions may be predicated' (PTX-9.3-NOT-013); (2) 'All instructions have an optional guard predicate ... prefix an instruction with @{!}p' (PTX-9.3-NOT-018); (3) the general predication form's explicit rule 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' and its Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-NOT-031/032); therefore a predicated not.b32 executes if and only if the complete guard expression is true, and does nothing (no state change) when the complete guard expression is false.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: The chain steps 1-3 are direct source facts; the concluding state-level reading 'no state change' of 'do nothing' is an interpretation, explicitly separated and subject to Gate B confirmation (see claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-035). Confidence 'medium' reflects that interpretive step.

semantic_claims.statement: The not Semantics block states, verbatim, 'd = ~a;'.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: The Semantics block is the family-level block for not (it accompanies the type set { .pred, .b16, .b32, .b64 }); for the bounded base unit only the .b32 instantiation is interpreted.

semantic_claims.statement: Bit-complement semantics: when not.b32 executes with a register source, the value written to the destination register d equals the bitwise complement of the value read from source a, computed over the 32-bit untyped .b32 value domain. This is derived from 'd = ~a;' (PTX-9.3-NOT-005), 'Bitwise negation; one's complement.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-002), 'Invert the bits in a.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-004), and the .b32 'Bits (untyped)' 32-bit type (PTX-9.3-NOT-021, PTX-9.3-NOT-023). The exact formal statement (representation of bitwise complement over the 32-bit bit-value domain) is a semantic-phase matter (OQ-8; claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-072).

Guard-true behavior: when the complete guard expression evaluates true (including the no-guard case), the instruction executes: the pre-instruction value of source operand a is read, and the destination register d is updated with the bitwise complement of that value. This is consistent with the general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-NOT-032).

Guard-false state effect: when the complete guard expression evaluates false, the represented consequence is that the instruction does not execute and no state component changes. This consequence is source-resolved: section 9.7.13.2 (Control Flow Instructions: @) explicitly states 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-031) and its Semantics line is 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-NOT-032); combined with the general rules that all PTX instructions may be predicated (PTX-9.3-NOT-013) and that all instructions have an optional guard predicate prefix @{!}p (PTX-9.3-NOT-018), the clause applies to the bounded base not.b32. The official do-nothing clause itself is SOURCE_FACT (PTX-NOT-SEM1-028); the state-level reading 'no state component changes' is the semantic interpretation of 'do nothing' and is subject to Gate B confirmation. This follows the mov.b32 Gate B lesson: the consequence is not presented as a human assumption.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: Confidence 'medium' because the claim includes the interpretive step 'no state component changes' as the state-level reading of 'do nothing'; the underlying official clause is quoted and verified (claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-028).

semantic_claims.statement: State read: the instruction reads source operand a. When a is a register, its current (pre-instruction) value is read from the value-register file; the description 'Invert the bits in a.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-004) and the Semantics 'd = ~a;' (PTX-9.3-NOT-005) require this read. Whether a may be a constant immediate is an open question (PTX-NOT-SEM1-066).

State read: when a guard is present, the value of the predicate register referenced by the guard is read to evaluate the complete guard expression. The general predication form of section 9.7.13.2 executes for threads whose guard predicate is True (PTX-9.3-NOT-031).

State write: when the instruction executes with a real destination register, the destination register d is updated with the bitwise complement of the value read from source a. The source states no other register write for the bounded base not.b32 form.

State write locality: only the destination update required by the bounded semantics is proposed; no memory state space, special-register state space, carry flag, status register, or condition-code component is written by the bounded base not.b32 (the base form has no such operands).
Static precondition PRE-1: the instruction type specifier .b32 is a valid bit-size fundamental type of 32-bit width.

Static precondition PRE-2: operands d and a are size-compatible with instruction type .b32 (32-bit operands), consistent with the family rule 'The size of the operands must match, but not necessarily the type.' and the bit-size compatibility rule.
Static precondition PRE-3: the destination operand d denotes a declared register variable in the .reg state space (or the bit bucket '_', applicability open question PTX-NOT-SEM1-067).
Static precondition PRE-4: the source operand a is a register variable; whether a may be a constant immediate is not evidenced in the not section (bundle GAP-1; claim PTX-NOT-SEM1-066).
Static precondition PRE-5: if a guard is present, it refers to a predicate register variable of type .pred in the register state space, optionally negated.
Static precondition PRE-6: base not (and therefore the bounded base not.b32 form) is introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.
No dynamic precondition is stated in the evidence for not.b32 (for example, no requirement on source operand values, and no flag or status-register requirement). None is asserted.

Determinism: the execution relation for not.b32 is deterministic for any well-formed state and well-typed instruction, because the value written is fully determined by the value read (a pure bitwise complement of a fixed 32-bit value, no arithmetic, no truncation, no rounding) and the guard evaluation is a deterministic function of the predicate register value. Determinism is NOT explicitly stated in the source (bundle GAP-3; architecture assumption A-3); this is a derived interpretation stated as proof obligation PRF-1.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: Confidence 'medium' because determinism is not explicitly stated in the source; the derivation is natural (a pure bit-wise operation), but the claim is not a quoted source fact.

semantic_claims.statement: PTX ISA Notes for not: 'Introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.'
Target ISA Notes for not: 'Supported on all target architectures.'
Version restriction: the base not.b32 form is introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0 (derived from the not-family PTX ISA Note of section 9.7.8.4, which applies to the not family including the .b32 form).

Target restriction: the base not.b32 form is supported on all target architectures (derived from the not-family Target ISA Note of section 9.7.8.4, which directly establishes the not-family target set; no target-set gap exists for the base form).

No explicit error, trap, or exceptional-behavior clause for not (or not.b32) was found in the evidence (bundle coverage area 15 status NOT_FOUND; GAP-4). The absence is not asserted as a positive source fact; no error, trap, or exceptional behavior is invented. Whether the absence means no such behaviors exist is unresolved.
No explicit undefined-behavior clause for not (or not.b32) was found in the evidence (GAP-4). No undefined-behavior claim is made; no undefined behavior is invented.
No explicit implementation-defined-behavior clause for not (or not.b32) was found in the evidence. No implementation-defined-behavior claim is made.
Section 5.2.2 restricts the .u8, .s8, and .b8 instruction types to ld, st, add, sub, min, max, neg, and cvt instructions; .b32 is not in the restricted list.

The sub-word-size restriction of section 5.2.2 does not restrict the .b32 instruction type; no .b32-specific restriction for not was found in the sections read (negative evidence; architecture assumption A-8).

Variable declaration rules: all storage for data is specified with variable declarations; a declaration names the state space, type and size, name, optional array size, optional initializer, and optional fixed address; predicate variables may only be declared in the register state space.
Parameterized variable names are supported: e.g., '.reg .b32 %r<100>;' declares %r0..%r99; the shorthand may be used with any fundamental type and any state space.

The special register (.sreg) state space holds predefined, platform-specific registers, such as grid, cluster, CTA, and thread parameters, clock counters, and performance monitoring registers; all special registers are predefined.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: The .sreg state space is not required by the bounded base not.b32 form (no sreg operand); recorded for completeness of the state-space picture.

semantic_claims.statement: Minimal machine state design (architecture D-5, D-14): the state for the bounded base not.b32 is the pair (value-register file, predicate-register file); no memory, special-register, or concurrency state is required by the base form's syntax and description.

Instruction representation design (architecture D-1, D-16): a not.b32 instruction is represented as an optional guard (@{!}p), mnemonic not, type specifier .b32, no modifier, destination operand d, and a single source operand a in that order.

Value domain design (architecture D-11, D-3): the value domain for .b32 is proposed as a fixed-width 32-bit untyped bit-value domain, because .b32 is the 'Bits (untyped)' basic type and the logic/shift family is described as fundamentally untyped, performing bit-wise operations on operands of any type of the same size.

Execution-semantics representation design (architecture D-25): the future execution semantics for not.b32 is designed to be represented as an execution relation between (state, instruction) and state, not merely as a function, so that determinism and frame/locality obligations are non-vacuous.

Execution-result representation design (architecture D-8): an instruction-local outcome has at least two cases: executed (with destination update) and guard-false (no state change, per derived interpretation PTX-NOT-SEM1-035); no error constructor is proposed because no explicit exceptional behavior for the bounded base not.b32 is evidenced (GAP-4).

Aliasing/read-before-write: because the semantics is a bitwise complement (d = ~a;), the value of a is read before the destination update; the official example 'not.b32  mask,mask;' (PTX-9.3-NOT-009) directly shows the destination and source may be the same register, in which case the register retains its pre-instruction value as the source of the complement.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: The same-register case is directly evidenced by the official example; the read-before-write ordering is the derived reading of 'd = ~a;'.

semantic_claims.statement: OQ-1/GAP-1: whether the source operand a of not.b32 may be a constant immediate is not explicitly evidenced in the not section (9.7.8.4); the not syntax, description, and examples use register operands only. Sibling family examples (or.b32 mask mask,0x00010001, PTX-9.3-NOT-011; xor.b16 d,x,0x0001;, PTX-9.3-NOT-012) show immediates in the same family but do not resolve the not-specific question (bundle do_not_infer: true).
OQ-2/GAP-2: whether the bit bucket '_' is permitted as the destination of the scalar not.b32 form; only the general section 9.2 rule exists (PTX-9.3-NOT-016).

OQ-4/GAP-7: whether the .pred, .b16, and .b64 forms of not (and the sibling logic/shift family instructions and, or, xor) should be modeled as separate later units; the bounded task covers only the scalar .b32 form (architecture D-0c).
OQ-5: the exact Lean encoding of the 1-bit predicate register value domain (PTX-9.3-NOT-023 states predicate registers are 1-bit) is a Lean-mapping decision for a later phase.

OQ-6: whether compilation-level register notes (spilling, function-scope/ABI restriction, legacy module-scope handling; PTX-9.3-NOT-023) impose constraints that a future program-level semantics must model; they are excluded from the instruction-local architecture.

OQ-7/GAP-5: how the family operand-typing rule 'The size of the operands must match, but not necessarily the type.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-006) should be formulated for not.b32 together with the bit-size compatibility rule (PTX-9.3-NOT-022): whether a register declared .u32, .s32, or .f32 is an acceptable operand for instruction type .b32, and how immediate values (if adopted) are typed under the same rules.

OQ-8: the exact Lean statement of the bit-complement fidelity candidate obligation PRF-7 ('the value written equals the bitwise complement of the value read', grounded in PTX-9.3-NOT-005 'd = ~a;'), including the representation of bitwise complement over the 32-bit bit-value domain, is a semantic-phase matter; the architecture records the candidate family only.

GAP-8: literal searches for '@p not', 'not.b64', 'not.b16', and 'not.b32 %' returned zero matches each; these negative results support no claims about predication of not (governed by the general rule PTX-9.3-NOT-013) and no claims about other not forms; the 'not.b32' matches are the not example (HTML line 14387) and the cnot.b32 example (HTML line 14420, a different instruction).

assumption_notes.statement: No ASSUMPTION-classified semantic claim remains in this artifact. The guard-false consequence was source-resolved by the bundle's section 9.7.13.2 evidence (PTX-9.3-NOT-031/032: 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' and 'If {!}p then instruction') and is classified DERIVED_INTERPRETATION (PTX-NOT-SEM1-035), with the official clause itself SOURCE_FACT (PTX-NOT-SEM1-028); this implements the mov.b32 Gate B lesson and the architecture's OQ-3 is resolved at the evidence level. Items that remain pending ordinary semantic gate confirmation are classified DERIVED_INTERPRETATION, DESIGN_DEPENDENCY, or OPEN_QUESTION rather than ASSUMPTION: determinism (PTX-NOT-SEM1-047, GAP-3), no-error outcome representation (PTX-NOT-SEM1-064, GAP-4), error/UB/implementation-defined absence (PTX-NOT-SEM1-052/053/054, GAP-4), negative literal-search results (PTX-NOT-SEM1-073, GAP-8), immediate source (PTX-NOT-SEM1-066, GAP-1), and bit-bucket destination (PTX-NOT-SEM1-067, GAP-2). The architecture assumptions A-1..A-10 were reviewed: A-1 (HTML authoritative; PDF not read in the architecture pass) is superseded at the bundle level because the source bundle records PDF reads performed during SOURCE_CURATION; A-2/A-5 are bounded-scope design choices carried as DESIGN_DEPENDENCY (PTX-NOT-SEM1-003/060); A-3 determinism is DERIVED (PTX-NOT-SEM1-047); A-4 guard-false is source-resolved (PTX-NOT-SEM1-035); A-6 error absence is OPEN_QUESTION (PTX-NOT-SEM1-052); A-7 predicate 1-bit/two-valued-domain encoding is deferred to Lean mapping (PTX-NOT-SEM1-069); A-8 sub-word-size negative evidence is DERIVED (PTX-NOT-SEM1-056); A-9 literal-search negative evidence is OPEN_QUESTION (PTX-NOT-SEM1-073); A-10 PRF-6 vacuity risk is carried in future_theorem_obligation_topics PRF-6.

ambiguities.description: The unit not.b32 is the scalar 32-bit bit-size form of the not instruction of section 9.7.8.4; the same section defines the .pred, .b16, and .b64 forms (PTX-9.3-NOT-003), and the family intro records that not also operates on predicates (PTX-9.3-NOT-010). The bounded base unit adopts only the .b32 scalar form; the other forms are recorded as source facts and deferred (architecture D-0c, OQ-4).

ambiguities.description: Whether the source operand a of not.b32 may be a constant immediate is not explicitly evidenced in the not section; the not syntax, description, and examples use register operands only, while sibling family examples (or, xor) show immediates (bundle GAP-1, do_not_infer: true).
ambiguities.impact: Non-blocking for the register-source base semantics; affects the exact set of well-formed source forms and static well-formedness of programs.

ambiguities.description: How the family operand-typing rule 'The size of the operands must match, but not necessarily the type.' combines with the bit-size compatibility rule for not.b32 operand typing (e.g., whether a register declared .u32, .s32, or .f32 is an acceptable operand for instruction type .b32) is not resolved (bundle GAP-5).

resolved_open_questions.summary: Architecture OQ-3 (guard-false consequence interpretation beyond 'controls conditional execution' needed human approval; mov.b32 Gate B lesson): RESOLVED at the evidence level in this artifact. The bundle includes the explicit official clause of section 9.7.13.2 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-NOT-031) with Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-NOT-032); the not.b32 guard-false consequence is DERIVED_INTERPRETATION (PTX-NOT-SEM1-035) and is no longer presented as a human assumption (zero ASSUMPTION claims). The state-level reading 'no state component changes' of 'do nothing' remains subject to ordinary Gate B confirmation.

future_theorem_obligation_topics.description: Determinism of the execution relation for not.b32: at most one resulting state for any well-formed state and well-typed instruction. Derived interpretation PTX-NOT-SEM1-047 (determinism not explicitly stated, GAP-3); grounded in the deterministic bitwise-complement operation and deterministic guard evaluation.

Destination-only update / frame: when not.b32 executes with a register destination, only the destination register may change; every other value register and predicate register is unchanged. Grounded in PTX-NOT-SEM1-038/039.

Bit-bucket discard: when the destination is '_', execution changes no value register. Depends on the general-rule-supported bit-bucket interpretation (AMB-3; PTX-NOT-SEM1-067); scalar not.b32-specific demonstration remains an open question, which is non-blocking for the base register-destination semantics.

Guard-false frame: when the complete guard expression evaluates false, the entire state is unchanged. Grounded in DERIVED_INTERPRETATION PTX-NOT-SEM1-035 (source-resolved via section 9.7.13.2 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.', PTX-9.3-NOT-031/032); the consequence is an evidence-backed derived interpretation and remains subject to the ordinary Gate B review of this semantics.

Guard-behavior: the instruction executes if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true, covering no-guard, @p, and @!p cases uniformly. Grounded in PTX-NOT-SEM1-022/031/034 and guard_semantics, now also the general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-NOT-032).

Result-domain membership: when not.b32 executes, the value written to the destination lies in the 32-bit bit-size value domain of .b32. DISPOSITION RECORDED (architecture-critic v1 F-3 / foundation-v2 A-10): PRF-6 may be definitionally vacuous under the proposed typed register-file representation; per the mov.b32 lesson, reclassification as a VAL-style definitional well-formedness obligation (rather than a semantic proof obligation) is recorded as the recommended disposition, with final adoption confirmed at the theorem-design stage (Gate C / theorem-strength gate).

Bit-complement fidelity (candidate): when the instruction executes with a register source, the value written to the destination equals the bitwise complement of the value read from the source ('d = ~a;', PTX-9.3-NOT-005). Meaningful semantic property for a bitwise-negation instruction; the exact formal statement (including the representation of bitwise complement over the 32-bit bit-value domain) is a semantic-phase matter (OQ-8; PTX-NOT-SEM1-072).
